generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL; generated rows use IDs above the compact maximum so compact rows are preserved; deduplicate before writing so the writer never rejects a row.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Sample from the parent table's primary-key pool; include NULL rows when the column is nullable; never write a value with no matching parent (declared FOREIGN KEY constraints must hold); deduplicate and validate against the parent pool before writing.
generic_sampling_rules.int_quantity: Positive integers; sample within [1, 100000000] unless a per-column range is given.
generic_sampling_rules.real_measure: Real numbers with one decimal place; sample within the per-column range; include boundary values at listed literals and one step (0.1) on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Short ASCII/Unicode strings; include near-variants (case changes, trailing characters) of listed equality literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_date: Dates in 'D Month YYYY' format (e.g. '18 February 1992'); sample across years 1990-2010.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For every nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; NULL share follows the compact database's share for that column, with a fallback share of 0.08 when the compact share is zero and a minimum of one NULL row per nullable column; applied last, after all boundary, tie, group and formula planting, and a planted NULL is never overwritten.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: About 20% of non-key text values are fresh near-variants; the rest are drawn from the observed pool.
generic_sampling_rules.row_count: Use table_sizes_per_instance exactly; no random size factor; every table receives at least one generated row per instance; the instance builder must produce exactly that many valid rows (deduplicate PKs and unique columns, validate FKs, never NULL a NOT NULL column) so rows_skipped is 0.
generic_sampling_rules.generation_order: Fill parent tables (city, match) before children (temperature, hosting_city); apply formulas, boundary, tie and group planting first, then plant NULLs last; after NULL planting, re-verify group sizes and boundary cases among non-NULL values and repair deterministically if disturbed.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports fk_violations: 32 across 19/20 instances, all flagged as new_integrity_failures, making 19/20 instances invalid. The design explicitly limits unmatched child FKs to hosting_city.Host_City and hosting_city.Match_ID, and says temperature.City_ID gets no FK violations. However _plant_unmatched() in instance.py writes fresh values (max(parent)+1) into *every* dependency whose (child,col) is in allowed_unmatched and also runs the 'parent row without children' rewrite for every dependency. More importantly, the unmatched-planting loop does not distinguish generated rows from the copied compact rows: writer.py appends generated rows to a copy of the compact DB, so if a parent table (city) has generated parents without a child, or a child FK is rewritten to a value not present in the *final* pool of parent values, the copied DB plus appended rows violate the declared FOREIGN KEY constraints. The 32 FK violations confirm that unmatching is being applied in a way that breaks referential integrity rather than just producing JOIN-miss rows that the specification intended as *semantic* unmatched rows (child FK that no longer matches) — but the schema declares FOREIGN KEY constraints, so writing non-existent parent keys into child columns is itself a constraint violation.
issues.requested_revision: Do not write child FK values that have no matching parent into columns governed by declared FOREIGN KEY constraints. Instead achieve the 'unmatched join rows' pattern by (a) keeping child FK NULL where the column is nullable (already handles join-miss via NULL), and (b) ensuring parent rows without children by not generating a referencing child row — never by inventing a non-existent parent key. Confirm with an integrity re-run that fk_violations is 0 in every instance.

issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback shows temperature.Mar: NULL 0/82, temperature.Jun: NULL 0/82, temperature.Oct: NULL 0/82. These are nullable REAL columns and are listed in null_targets, so the interface rule 'each instance contains generated rows with NULL and rows with non-NULL' is not met for these columns. Root cause: _plant_nulls() runs before _plant_comparison_boundaries(), and the comparison-boundary planting skips positions where the source value is None but then overwrites the *target* column at index i only if source is non-NULL; conversely, where target was NULL it remains NULL only if not overwritten. The feedback shows Mar/Jun/Oct end with zero NULLs, meaning boundary planting overwrote all their planted NULLs. Per interface note, 'generated rows: NULL 0/n' may be noted but does not block a pass; however it signals the NULL planting order is fragile and conflicting with boundary planting for exactly the columns flagged above.
issues.requested_revision: Plant comparison boundaries first, then plant NULLs last (or make boundary planting never overwrite a NULL target). Verify that Mar, Jun, Oct (and all nullable columns) each show at least one generated NULL row.

issues.evidence: _plant_ties() in instance.py ignores the requested ranks argument and hardcodes [1, 3] regardless of what the spec requests; per_column_exceptions for city.Regional_Population and city.GDP specify tie_at_rank [1,3] which happens to match, so this is not currently a correctness defect but is a latent bug. Separately, the tie verification uses a DESC sort keyed on '-(v if numeric else 0)', which for non-numeric values collapses to 0 and can produce incorrect tie placement if used on text columns. issues.evidence: _plant_group_sizes() is called for the (hosting_city, Host_City) exception but ignores which values are already present and overwrites positions 0..5 with base1/base2/base3 chosen from existing non-NULL values. issues.requested_revision: Reorder specification application: formulas and boundary/tie/group planting first, then _plant_nulls last; and choose group base values guaranteed distinct from each other and from non-group rows.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows rows_skipped is large and non-zero for every table: city 134, match 76, temperature 69, hosting_city 79 skipped, versus rows_added city 78, match 26, temperature 44, hosting_city 15. The specification requires table_sizes_per_instance exactly (city 13, match 6, temperature 8, hosting_city 6) and 'every table receives at least one generated row per instance'. With 20 instances the expected added rows would be city 260, match 120, temperature 160, hosting_city 120; the actual added counts are far below that, and the skipped counts show that most generated rows are being rejected by the writer (writer.py falls back to row-by-row and counts failures). The cause is that instance.py generates rows with duplicate primary keys / unique values and FK values that violate constraints, and writer.py rejects them instead of the instance builder guaranteeing validity. This means the per-instance table sizes are not actually met.
issues.requested_revision: Make the instance builder produce exactly table_sizes_per_instance valid rows per table (deduplicate PKs and unique columns before writing, ensure FK values reference existing parents, and ensure NOT NULL columns are never NULL). The writer should not be the mechanism that enforces sizes; rows_skipped should be 0 for all tables. Re-run and confirm rows_added equals table_sizes_per_instance * n_instances and rows_skipped is 0.

issues.evidence: The specification requires for temperature.Mar comparison_boundary: 'equal to and one step (0.1) from Jul and Oct; both equal and one-step-above/below cases occur per instance', and similarly for Feb/Jun/Mar, Jun/Feb/Oct, Jul/Mar, Oct/Mar/Jun, Nov/Mar, Dec/Mar. In instance.py `_plant_comparison_boundaries` only plants a single equal value and a single ±0.1 value per pair, chosen at random indices, and it does not guarantee that both the equal case and the one-step-above and one-step-below cases occur per instance. It also does not guarantee that the compound predicates (Mar < Jul OR Mar > Oct) and (Jun < Oct OR Mar < Jun) are both true and false across instances. The construction_pairs feedback shows only 25 of 39 eligible pairs separated, which is consistent with the boundary planting not being deterministic/complete.
issues.requested_revision: Plant the comparison boundaries deterministically: for each specified pair, ensure at least one row has the two columns equal, at least one row has the second column one step (0.1) above, and at least one row has it one step below, per instance. Also explicitly plant rows making the compound predicates (Mar < Jul OR Mar > Oct) and (Jun < Oct OR Mar < Jun) both true and false. Do not rely on random index selection.

issues.evidence: The specification requires city.Regional_Population comparison_boundary values at 4999998, 4999999, 5000000, 5000001, 9813638, 9813639, 9813640, 9999999, 10000000, 10000001, and city.Hanzi values '上海' and '上海x', and match.Competition values '1994 FIFA World Cup qualification' and '1994 fifa world cup qualification'. In spec.py `_parse_boundary_targets` only extracts numeric literals from a dict target with a 'values' key; the specification's targets for these columns are given as strings (e.g. 'Values at 4999998, ...' and "Values '上海' and '上海x'"), so `_parse_boundary_targets` returns an empty list for Regional_Population and the string targets are only parsed by `_parse_string_targets` for comparison_boundary exceptions. For Regional_Population the targets string is 'Values at 4999998, ...' which `_parse_string_targets` will not extract (no quoted strings), so the boundary literals are never added to the literal pool. Similarly the Hanzi and Competition string targets are parsed only if the targets is a string with quoted values; the specification uses "Values '上海' and '上海x'" which does contain quotes, so those may be parsed, but the numeric boundary values for Regional_Population are not.
issues.requested_revision: Extend `_parse_boundary_targets` to also extract numeric literals from string target descriptions (e.g. via the existing `_NUM` regex on the string), so that the Regional_Population boundary values are added to the literal pool. Verify that the boundary values appear in generated rows.

issues.evidence: The specification requires city.City duplicates_for_distinct with duplicate share 20-50% so DISTINCT reduces the row count. The `drop_unique_duplicates` function only drops duplicates for unique columns, and city.City is not unique. There is no code that ensures a 20-50% duplicate share for city.City.

issues.evidence: The specification requires hosting_city.Host_City group_sizes: 'Three distinct groups: one value appearing exactly once, one appearing exactly twice, one appearing three or more times, using distinct base values chosen from existing non-NULL city.City_ID values.' The program's `_plant_group_sizes` uses `existing[0], existing[1], existing[2]` from the column's own values, which for hosting_city.Host_City are FK values drawn from city.City_ID, so they are existing city IDs. However, the function requires n >= 6 and only plants if there are at least 3 distinct existing values; with table size 6 for hosting_city this is borderline, and the function overwrites vals[0..5] which may conflict with the FK consistency and NULL planting. More importantly, the specification also requires hosting_city.Host_City unmatched_join_rows via NULL FK, and the NULL planting happens after group planting, so the group sizes may be disturbed by NULLs. The execution feedback shows hosting_city.Host_City NULL 4/19, which is a high share and may break the group size requirement.

The specification per_column_exceptions for temperature.Mar/Feb/Jun/Jul/Oct/Nov/Dec require 'equal to and one step (0.1) from' each referenced column, i.e. equal, +0.1 and -0.1 per pair. The 'step' value parsed by spec._parse_relative_pairs is ignored in the planting loop (the loop variable `step` is unused).
issues.requested_revision: Plant all three cases per pair: for each referenced column, write one row with c = other, one with c = other + 0.1, one with c = other - 0.1 (using the parsed step). Use distinct rows so the three cases are simultaneously present, and ensure the referenced column value is not itself overwritten by a later pair in a way that breaks the relation (or re-verify after all pairs are planted).

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_compound_predicates hard-codes Mar/Jul/Oct and Jun/Oct/Mar values (1.0/2.0/3.0, 5.0/4.0/6.0) on rows 0-3 unconditionally. This runs AFTER _plant_comparison_boundaries in the same loop iteration order (boundaries are planted inside the per-exception loop, compound predicates after the loop), so it overwrites the boundary plantings on rows 0-3 for Mar, Jul, Oct, Jun. The specification requires both the boundary pairs and the compound predicates to hold; the current ordering makes them mutually destructive on the same rows.
issues.requested_revision: Plant compound-predicate witnesses on rows disjoint from the boundary-pair rows (e.g. reserve the last rows of the table for compound predicates, or track used row indices), and re-verify both the boundary relations and the compound-predicate truth values after all planting. Also make the compound-predicate planting respect the boundary pairs (e.g. choose values that satisfy both where possible, or use separate rows).

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_group_sizes requires n >= 6 and uses existing[0..2] as base values, then writes vals[0]=base1, vals[1]=vals[2]=base2, vals[3..5]=base3. For hosting_city the specification size is 6, so this is exactly at the threshold; but _plant_nulls runs afterwards and may NULL some of rows 0-5 (hosting_city.Host_City is a null target), which the code comment claims is avoided ('plant on rows that will not be overwritten by NULL planting') but _plant_nulls samples uniformly at random with no exclusion of the group rows. Execution feedback shows hosting_city.Host_City NULL 14/22, so group rows are at risk. The specification requires group sizes 1, 2, >=3 to survive NULL planting and be re-verified.
issues.requested_revision: Exclude the group-planted row indices from _plant_nulls (pass a protected-index set), or re-verify and repair group sizes among non-NULL values after NULL planting as the specification's generation_order rule requires ('after NULL planting, re-verify group sizes and boundary cases among non-NULL values and repair deterministically if disturbed').

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_duplicates copies existing[i % len(existing)] into vals[0..target-1], which can overwrite PK-adjacent or unique-constrained values and, more importantly, runs before _plant_nulls but after PK/unique dedup, so it can reintroduce duplicate unique values (city.City is not unique here, so this is benign for city, but the pattern is applied generically). More concretely, the duplicate planting targets city.City with share 20-50%; execution feedback does not report a DISTINCT-reduction check, and the specification requires 'Duplicate share 20-50% so DISTINCT reduces the row count'. The current implementation copies values but does not verify the resulting duplicate share is in [0.2, 0.5] after NULL planting (NULLs reduce the non-NULL duplicate share).
issues.requested_revision: After NULL planting, compute the duplicate share among non-NULL city.City values and repair deterministically if it falls outside 20-50% (e.g. by copying additional non-NULL values). Also ensure duplicate planting does not violate any unique constraint by re-running drop_unique_duplicates or by restricting duplicate planting to non-unique columns.

issues.evidence: instance.py _ensure_parents_without_children only rewrites a child FK when childset >= set(parent); it does not guarantee that at least one parent row has no child when the child table is small (hosting_city size 6, match size 6). With 6 child rows and 6 parent rows, it is possible (and likely) that every parent has a child, violating the specification's unmatched_join_rows target for city.City_ID and match.Match_ID ('Parent rows without children'). Execution feedback does not report a check for this, and construction_pairs separated = 23/39 suggests several targets are not separated.
issues.requested_revision: Deterministically reserve at least one parent key that no child row references: after filling child FKs, pick a parent key not in the child set (or rewrite one child FK to a different existing parent key) so that at least one parent row has no child, for both city (vs temperature and hosting_city) and match (vs hosting_city). Verify this explicitly and add it to the construction checks.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions for temperature.Mar/Feb/Jun/Jul/Oct/Nov/Dec describe relative boundary targets ('equal to and one step (0.1) from Jul and Oct', etc.) but do not state which rows or how many rows must carry each case, nor how to reconcile them with the compound_predicate targets on the same columns. The compound_predicate targets for Mar and Jun ('Make (Mar < Jul OR Mar > Oct) both true and false across instances') are stated per-instance, but the boundary targets are stated per-instance too, and the two sets of constraints can conflict on the same rows. The specification should state the precedence or the disjoint-row requirement.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the specification that boundary-pair witnesses and compound-predicate witnesses must be planted on disjoint rows (or state a precedence), and state the minimum number of rows per case (e.g. one row per (column, other, step) triple). This removes the ambiguity that led the engineer to overwrite boundary rows with compound-predicate values.

issues.evidence: The specification's null_targets includes city.City, city.Hanzi, city.Hanyu_Pinyin, city.Regional_Population, city.GDP, match.Date, match.Venue, match.Score, match.Result, match.Competition, and all temperature month columns, but the compact database's NULL share is 0.0 for all of them (per the specification's own uncertainty note). The fallback share of 0.08 with a minimum of one NULL row is applied, which is fine, but the specification does not state whether the duplicate-share (20-50%) and group-size (1,2,>=3) targets are computed over all rows or only non-NULL rows. The engineer's _plant_duplicates and _plant_group_sizes operate before NULL planting, so the targets are computed over all rows, but NULL planting then reduces the non-NULL share. The specification should state the denominator.
issues.requested_revision: State explicitly whether duplicates_for_distinct and group_sizes targets are evaluated over all rows or over non-NULL rows only, and whether they must be re-verified after NULL planting. This determines whether the engineer's current pre-NULL planting is correct or must be followed by a repair step.
